title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: Abraham justified by faith — no path to Adam-imputation
pass_a_gloss: To firm that reason of yours you cite the Apostle proving Abraham was justified because he believed God, and it was imputed to him for righteousness. Who would ever have hoped from that to get Adam's first actual sin immediately imputed to all humans—and indeed unto this penalty, hereditary corruption? For that is our question, whose affirmation you had formally to conclude. You must be a subtle and wondrous craftsman of arguments who can forge that imputation from such places.
pass_b_english: To firm this reason of yours you cite the Apostle's reasoning proving that Abraham was justified because he believed God, and it was imputed to him for righteousness. Who would ever have hoped that from there it could be effected that Adam's first actual sin is immediately imputed to all humans, and indeed unto this penalty, namely hereditary corruption? For this is our question, whose affirmation was formally to be concluded by you. You must indeed be subtle, and a wondrous craftsman of arguments, who can fashion that imputation from places of this kind.
source_text: Ad firmandam hanc tuam rationem citas ratiocinationem Apostoli probantis Abrahamum fuisse justificatum, quia credidit Deo, & imputatum est ei ad justitiam. Quis unquam sperasset inde posse effici, primum peccatum actuale Adami omnibus hominibus imputari immediate, & quidem ad hanc poenam, corruptionem scilicet haereditariam? Nam haec est nostra quaestio, cujus affirmatio tibi formaliter concludenda fuit. Subtilem profecto te esse oportet, ac mirum artificem argumentorum, qui ex huiusmodi locis conficere illam imputationem possis.

lemmas.gloss: it was imputed to him for righteousness

choices.choice: Faith imputed for righteousness ≠ path to Adam immediate imputation
